reason: Confirmed on every point. round30/report.json next_focus (4) says 'keep the hourly rounds at 07:13-11:13Z read-only, or skip them'. The CONTEXT 02:02Z entry (items 1-5) has no round-schedule clause. The live timer.sh processes (Win32_Process) for 07:13, 08:13, 09:13 and 10:13Z all say 'launch the next research round unless one is running.' The blocking mechanism is logged in CONTEXT 28 Sep 20:13Z: crons fire only when the session is idle, rounds were lost to a busy session, and timer notifications are 'queued until the session is free'. A full round takes ~27 min (round 30 ran 01:13-01:40Z). So an 08:13Z round would hold the session until ~08:40Z, over the tail of the exp89p read window (07:38-08:35Z), the last 08:40Z header and the 08:45Z A-M1 cutoff. It could turn a '+' read into a late one, which means UNUSED. It would also push exp89l's CI read (08:45Z + ~10.9 h = ~19:39Z) further past the 18:37Z card. A 07:13Z round overlaps the 07:23Z prep, and the 09:13/10:13Z rounds overlap the exp75/exp89r reads and the A-M2 decision. The clause costs nothing: R8 bars new mechanisms after 02:00Z, and an E10 copy now needs the user's yes, so a full round at these hours has ~0 actionable output, and the read-only check still inspects the E10 file. The clause is ops-only and pre-score, and it changes no decision rule (R1-R10 untouched). Two small inaccuracies, neither of which refutes the finding. (a) There is no 11:13Z hourly timer. The round after A-M2 is the tail of the 11:10Z M2 timer ('...submit by 11:30 UTC ...; then launch the hourly research round if none is running'), which is already sequenced after M2. (b) The 06:07Z post-wake timer can also launch a round (only if none ran since 05:13Z). It needs a start cap so that it ends before the 07:23Z prep.
fix: Append to the PC31-01 CONTEXT line (pre-score): 'ROUND SCHEDULE 29 Sep: the hourly timers at 07:13, 08:13, 09:13 and 10:13Z mean in-session read-only checks only (<= 5 min: newest poll header, newest e10_watch file, newest feed digest; no workflow, no subagents, no extra Kaggle API calls). The round in the 06:07Z post-wake step starts only if it is before 06:45Z, and only if none ran since 05:13Z. The next full round is the one at the tail of the 11:10Z M2 timer, and it launches only after A-M2 is submitted or logged UNUSED. Decision headers, read watchers and the 07:23Z prep / 08:30Z / 11:10Z timers take precedence over any round. Timer texts are pointers; this line governs.' Do not re-arm or kill the timers; redirect via CONTEXT (as for the stale waiters).
realistic_gain: Operational only, with no direct score effect. It protects A-M1 (exp89l) from turning UNUSED through a late read in the ~08:13-08:40Z overlap. It also keeps exp89l's CI read as early as possible relative to the 18:37Z card, and keeps the A-M2 submit prompt. The expected value is small, but the cost is zero and it removes a plausible loss of the 29 Sep morning slot.
